steps: Identify the angle relationship (straight line, triangle, parallel lines, polygon, etc.)
Write the equation using the angle fact
Check your answer makes sense (positive, less than 360°)
method_card.title: Angle Facts & Properties
method_card.content:
Angles on a straight line add up to \(180°\). Angles around a point add up to \(360°\). Vertically opposite angles are equal.

Angles in a triangle add up to \(180°\). Angles in a quadrilateral add up to \(360°\). The interior angle sum of an \(n\)-sided polygon is \((n-2) \times 180°\).

Parallel lines: Alternate angles (Z-angles) are equal. Co-interior angles (C-angles) add up to \(180°\). Corresponding angles (F-angles) are equal.
method_card.example:
Find angle \(x\): Two angles on a straight line are \(x\) and \(130°\).

\(x + 130 = 180\)

\(x = 50°\)

gold.display: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An angle of \(3x + 15\) and a corresponding angle of \(5x - 25\) are formed. Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Corresponding angles are equal: 3x + 15 = 5x − 25 → 40 = 2x → x = 20.

gold.display: The interior angle of a regular polygon is 5 times its exterior angle. How many sides does it have?

misconceptions.message: Interior + exterior = 180°. If interior = 5 × exterior: 5e + e = 180 → e = 30°. Sides = 360 ÷ 30 = 12.

gold.display: Angles \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are at a point. \(a : b : c = 2 : 3 : 4\). Find angle \(b\).

misconceptions.message: Total = 360°. Sum of ratio parts = 9. One part = 360 ÷ 9 = 40°. b = 3 × 40 = 120°.

gold.display: A triangle has angles in the ratio \(3 : 4 : 5\). What is the largest angle?

misconceptions.message: Sum of parts = 12. One part = 180 ÷ 12 = 15°. Largest angle = 5 × 15 = 75°.

bronze.display: Two angles on a straight line are \(x\) and \(115°\). Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Angles on a straight line add to 180°, not 360°. So x = 180 − 115 = 65°.

bronze.display: Three angles around a point are \(120°\), \(85°\) and \(x\). Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Angles around a point add to 360°, not 180°. x = 360 − 120 − 85 = 155°.
360 − 120 − 85 = 155°. Check your subtraction.

bronze.display: Two vertically opposite angles are \(3x + 10\) and \(70°\). Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Vertically opposite angles are equal, not supplementary. 3x + 10 = 70, so x = 20.

bronze.display: A triangle has angles \(40°\), \(75°\) and \(x\). Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Angles in a triangle add to 180°, not 360°. x = 180 − 40 − 75 = 65°.

bronze.display: Find the exterior angle of a regular hexagon.

misconceptions.message: Exterior angle = 360 ÷ n = 360 ÷ 6 = 60°. You found the interior angle (120°).
Exterior angle of a regular polygon = 360° ÷ number of sides = 360 ÷ 6 = 60°.

bronze.display: A quadrilateral has angles \(90°\), \(80°\), \(110°\) and \(x\). Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Angles in a quadrilateral add to 360°. x = 360 − 90 − 80 − 110 = 80°.

bronze.display: Two angles on a straight line are \(2x\) and \(3x + 30\). Find \(x\).
Find the interior angle of a regular pentagon.

misconceptions.message: Interior angle sum = (5−2) × 180 = 540°. Each angle = 540 ÷ 5 = 108°.

silver.display: Two angles in a triangle are \(55°\) and \(x\). The exterior angle at the third vertex is \(130°\). Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Exterior angle = sum of opposite interior angles. 130 = 55 + x, so x = 75°.

silver.display: A regular polygon has an interior angle of \(156°\). How many sides does it have?

misconceptions.message: Exterior angle = 180 − 156 = 24°. Number of sides = 360 ÷ 24 = 15.
First find the exterior angle: 180 − 156 = 24°. Then divide: 360 ÷ 24 = 15 sides.

silver.display: Lines AB and CD are parallel. Angle ABE = \(65°\). Angle BEF = \(x\). BEF and ABE are alternate angles. Find \(x\).

misconceptions.message: Alternate angles are equal (not supplementary). x = 65°.

silver.display: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A co-interior angle is \(72°\). Find the other co-interior angle.

misconceptions.message: Co-interior angles are supplementary (add to 180°), not equal. 180 − 72 = 108°.

silver.display: The angles in a pentagon are \(x\), \(2x\), \(3x\), \(90°\) and \(120°\). Find \(x\).
An isosceles triangle has one angle of \(50°\). This is one of the equal angles. Find the other angle.

misconceptions.message: The two equal angles are both 50°. Third angle = 180 − 50 − 50 = 80°.
Two equal angles of 50° each. Remaining = 180 − 100 = 80°.
